elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once in any 12-month period.
elements.evidence: The clause permits inspection “not more than once per year,” which could allow two inspections within a rolling 12-month period if they occur in different calendar years.

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 30 days’ prior written notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires “no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice.”

elements.element: Audits must occur during Customer’s normal business hours.
elements.evidence: The inspection is limited to “the Company’s normal business hours.”

elements.element: The audit must be conducted by an independent auditor.
elements.evidence: The right is granted to HDI’s General Manager, not to an independent auditor.

elements.element: The auditor must be bound by confidentiality obligations.
elements.evidence: No confidentiality obligation applies to the inspecting party.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5%.
elements.evidence: HDI bears all inspection fees, without shifting costs to the Company even where underpayment exceeds 5%; this is more protective of the Company.

elements.element: The audit right must not permit direct access to Customer systems.
elements.evidence: The clause permits inspection of Company records but does not expressly prohibit direct access to Company systems or prescribe a non-system-access method.

elements.element: Audits may occur no more than once per year.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly limits inspection to “not more than once per year.”

elements.element: Customer must receive at least 15 days’ prior notice.
elements.evidence: The clause requires 30 days’ prior written notice, exceeding the 15-day minimum.

elements.element: Vendor must bear the audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 10%.
elements.evidence: HDI bears all inspection fees, without shifting costs to the Company even where underpayment exceeds 10%; this is more protective of the Company.

result.reason: The redline minimally adds the annual frequency cap needed to reach the fallback while retaining the existing, more protective 30-day notice and HDI-borne-cost provisions. It does not reach the preferred position because “once per year” is not a rolling 12-month restriction, HDI’s General Manager is not an independent confidential auditor, and direct system access is not prohibited. Drafting quality is reduced by the awkward construction “may ... have the right,” unnecessary comma placement, and ambiguity in “per year.”
